finding.claim: GET /rss passes the attacker-controlled query parameter u directly to URI.open, which fetches arbitrary http(s) URLs (including internal addresses and cloud metadata) and returns the first 400 bytes of the response body to the caller.

trace.note: get "/rss" route; query parameter u is attacker-controlled
params[:u] passed to URI.open with no scheme, host, port, or IP validation; .read fetches the body
data[0, 400] returns the response body to the attacker (non-blind SSRF)
TRUSTED allow-list is defined but never applied on this route

finding.guards_checked: No allow-list, scheme restriction, private/loopback/link-local IP block, port restriction, DNS pinning, or redirect control on this path. open-uri follows redirects by default. URI.open also falls back to File.open for non-URL strings and opens file:// URIs, so local file read is a related issue (not SSRF proper). Ruled out: /trusted (app.rb:12-16) validates the same parsed URI it fetches, uses exact host match, and Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects; /version (app.rb:18-20) uses a hardcoded URL.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /rss route (app.rb:7-10) has no scheme, host, IP, or port check before URI.open(params[:u]).read at app.rb:8. The TRUSTED allow-list at app.rb:5 is never referenced on this route. The only guard in the file, the host check at app.rb:14, belongs to /trusted, which is a separate route.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled params[:u] flows unvalidated from app.rb:7 into URI.open at app.rb:8, and data[0, 400] at app.rb:9 returns the fetched body to the caller, so this is a non-blind SSRF with no closing guard.
